docs.text:
I create clear, structured, and maintainable technical documentation that helps readers understand equipment, systems, procedures, and software interfaces.

With a professional background in oil and gas engineering and wellhead services, I bring practical technical knowledge to documentation involving equipment operation, installation, testing, commissioning, troubleshooting, and safety systems.

I am building my technical writing portfolio around documentation-as-code, structured content, and API documentation, with an interest in remote opportunities where technical accuracy, clarity, and organization matter.

docs.title: How I Approach Documentation
docs.text:
1. Understand the audience — identify the reader, their task, and the information they need.
  2. Organize the content — structure information with consistent headings, terminology, tables, and examples.
  3. Write clearly — make technical concepts easier to understand without losing important detail.
  4. Verify the content — check links, formatting, examples, and consistency against available source information.
  5. Maintain the documentation — use version control and repeatable publishing workflows where appropriate.

docs.title: Important Notice
docs.text: Portfolio examples are provided for demonstration and learning purposes. The API examples are illustrative and do not represent a verified live service. Engineering procedures and safety-critical information must be checked against approved technical documentation and applicable work procedures before operational use.

docs.title: 1. Document Control
docs.text:
• Document ID: SOP-OPS-WH-10K-001
  • Version: 2.0
  • Effective Date: October 2026
  • Manufacturer Spec: Cameron Specialty Multi-Bowl System (MN-S)
  • Author: Drilling & Completions Engineering Team

docs.title: 2. Objective & Scope
docs.text: This procedure outlines the technical and safety steps required to safely land, align, test, and secure a surface wellhead assembly. This applies to API 10,000 psi rated multi-bowl systems that housing both the surface casing hanger and intermediate casing strings within a single-piece compact body to minimize BOP removal steps.

docs.title: 3. HSE Requirements & Hazards
docs.text: ⚠️ CRITICAL SAFETY NOTE: All operations must be performed under an active Permit to Work (PTW). Ensure Gas Testing is completed before any hot work or welding begins.

docs.title: Key Hazards
docs.text:
• Suspended Loads: High risk during the hoisting and landing of heavy compact spools.
  • Trapped Pressure: Risk of trapped pressure below old wellhead sections or temporary caps.
  • Hot Work: Sparks and flames during casing cutting and wellhead welding.

docs.title: Required PPE
docs.text:
• Standard site PPE (hard hat, steel-toe boots, safety glasses, coveralls).
  • High-impact gloves for handling tools and heavy equipment.
  • Welding hood and leather jacket (if a welded connection is chosen).

docs.title: 4. Required Tools & Equipment
docs.text:
• [ ] Cameron API 6A 10,000 psi Compact Multi-Bowl Wellhead Housing
  • [ ] High-capacity hydraulic casing cutter (or mechanical cutting saw)
  • [ ] Hydraulic flange bolt torque wrench (calibrated up to 5,000 ft-lbs)
  • [ ] Manufacturer-specific running tool / landing joint / lifting eyes
  • [ ] High-pressure test pump and digital chart recorder
  • [ ] Non-destructive testing (NDT) dye penetrant kit
  • [ ] Original Cameron elastomeric / metal-to-metal "P-seals"

docs.title: Step 1: Preparation & Casing Cut-Off
docs.text:
1. Isolate the well: Ensure the well is completely dead, stable, and monitored for pressure or fluid influx.
  2. Expose the casing: Clean the surface casing string of cement, scale, and debris.
  3. Measure and mark: Mark the exact cut-off height on the conductor or surface casing based on the rig floor reference level.
  4. Execute the cut: Perform the rough and final cuts using a hydraulic casing cutter to ensure a smooth, perfectly horizontal face.
  5. Bevel the casing: Bevel the outer and inner edges of the casing to protect the wellhead internal seals from damage during landing.

docs.title: Step 2: Inspection & Seal Preparation
docs.text:
• Inspect the casing head ring grooves for any scratches or pitting.
  • Thoroughly clean the internal elastomeric seals and lubricate them with an approved manufacturer-specified grease.
  • Verify the casing outside diameter (OD) matches the wellhead slip-on/welding bore specification.

docs.title: Step 3: Landing the Casing Head (A-Section)
docs.text:
1. Attach approved lifting eyes and slings to the casing head.
  2. Slowly hoist the housing using the rig floor winch or crane.
  3. Lower the casing head smoothly over the casing stub.
    • Note: Ensure the side outlets align with the planned flowline or choke manifold orientation.
  4. Verify that the housing sits completely level using a precision spirit level.

docs.title: Step 4: Securing the Connection (Welded or Slip-On)
docs.text: Depending on the specific wellhead design, execute one of the following methods:

docs.title: Option A: Welded Type
docs.text:
• Preheat the casing and wellhead base according to welding procedures.
  • Apply the structural root pass and filler passes.
  • Allow the weld to cool slowly. Do not quench with water.

docs.title: Option B: Slip-on / Set-Screw Type
docs.text: • Tighten the external set-screws crosswise to the manufacturer's recommended torque values.

docs.title: Step 5: Pressure Testing
docs.text:
1. Connect the hydraulic test pump to the wellhead test port.
  2. Energize the internal seals by pumping clean water or hydraulic fluid.
  3. Hold a Low Pressure test at 250 psi for 5 minutes.
  4. Ramp up to the High Pressure test (10,000 psi) for 15 minutes.
  5. Record the results on a digital chart recorder; verify there is zero pressure drop.

docs.title: 6. Contingency & Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Potential Cause Remedial Action Pressure test failure Damaged O-ring or seal Depressurize system, change out seal, re-clean, and re-test. Wellhead not level Uneven casing cut-off Lift wellhead, re-grind the casing stub level, and re-seat. Flange bolt misalignment Rotational misalignment Use aligning pins before setting the full weight of the spool.

docs.title: 7. Sign-Off & Documentation
docs.text:
• [ ] Capture serial numbers of all installed seals and housings.
  • [ ] Append the pressure test chart to this document.
  • [ ] Hand over signed-off document to the Drilling Superintendent.

docs.title: Wellhead Telemetry API Reference
docs.text:
This reference documents an illustrative REST API for retrieving wellhead telemetry data. It demonstrates API documentation practices for endpoint definitions, authentication, request parameters, JSON responses, error handling, and rate limits.

Demonstration API

This is a portfolio example, not a verified or deployed API. The base URL, credentials, responses, rate limits, and endpoint behaviour are illustrative. Requests will not retrieve live well data. Do not use these examples for operational or safety-critical decisions.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text: The example API represents a service that provides telemetry readings associated with a wellhead monitoring system.

docs.title: Intended audience
docs.text:
• Software developers integrating telemetry data into an application
  • Technical teams reviewing a monitoring API
  • Engineers and documentation specialists evaluating the example interface

docs.title: Example capabilities
docs.text:
• Request telemetry for a specified rig
  • Review pressure and temperature readings
  • Inspect the reported telemetry status
  • Handle invalid requests and authentication errors

docs.title: 2. Base URL
docs.text:
The reserved .invalid domain below is used to prevent the example from being mistaken for a live service.

https://api.example.invalid
Property Description API style REST Data format JSON Example API version v1 Authentication model Bearer token Transport HTTPS in the illustrative design

docs.title: 3. Authentication
docs.text:
The example uses a Bearer token in the HTTP Authorization header.

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_EXAMPLE_TOKEN

YOUR_EXAMPLE_TOKEN is a placeholder, not a working credential. No token issuance or validation service is provided by this portfolio example.

docs.title: Authentication requirements
docs.text:
• Include the token in the Authorization header.
  • Do not place credentials in query parameters.
  • Avoid committing real credentials to source control.
  • A real implementation should use an approved token provisioning and rotation process.

An unauthenticated or invalidly authenticated request is illustrated as returning 401 Unauthorized.

docs.title: 4. Retrieve telemetry
docs.text: Returns an illustrative telemetry record for the requested rig.

docs.title: Request parameters
docs.text: Parameter Location Type Required Description rig_id Query String Yes Identifier of the rig whose telemetry is requested

docs.title: Example request
docs.text:
curl --get "https://api.example.invalid/v1/sensors/telemetry" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_EXAMPLE_TOKEN" \
  --header "Accept: application/json" \
  --data-urlencode "rig_id=RIG-001"

This command illustrates the request format only. The reserved host does not provide a live API service.

docs.title: Example successful response
docs.text:
Illustrative HTTP status: 200 OK

{
  "timestamp": "2026-10-20T10:30:00Z",
  "rig_id": "RIG-001",
  "pressure_psi": 1250.5,
  "temperature_f": 178.4,
  "status": "normal"
}

docs.title: Response fields
docs.text:
Field Type Description timestamp String (date-time) Example timestamp for the reading, represented in UTC rig_id String Identifier associated with the requested rig pressure_psi Number Illustrative pressure reading in pounds per square inch temperature_f Number Illustrative temperature reading in degrees Fahrenheit status String Example status label associated with the telemetry record

The example values are fictional and do not represent actual operating conditions or approved alarm thresholds.

docs.title: 5. HTTP status codes and error handling
docs.text:
The following responses illustrate how a real implementation could communicate common request failures.

Status code Meaning Example cause 200 OK Request succeeded A telemetry record is returned 400 Bad Request Request is invalid Required rig_id is missing or malformed 401 Unauthorized Authentication failed Token is missing, invalid, or expired 429 Too Many Requests Rate limit exceeded Request quota has been exceeded

docs.title: Example error response
docs.text:
Illustrative HTTP status: 400 Bad Request

{
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_REQUEST",
    "message": "The rig_id query parameter is required."
  }
}

This is a proposed error format for the demonstration. It is not a confirmed response from a live service.

docs.title: Troubleshooting guidance
docs.text:
400 Bad Request

Check that rig_id is present, correctly spelled, and supplied as a query parameter.

401 Unauthorized

Check that the Authorization header uses the Bearer scheme and that a valid token has been supplied. This example does not issue or validate tokens.

429 Too Many Requests

Stop sending requests temporarily and follow the retry guidance provided by the actual service, if available. A production API should document whether it provides Retry-After and rate-limit headers.

docs.title: 6. Rate limits
docs.text:
The previous portfolio example specified a limit of 1,000 requests per hour per API key.

This figure is illustrative only. It has not been verified against a live service.

A production API should document:

  • The applicable quota and its time window
  • Whether limits apply per user, token, or API key
  • The response returned when a quota is exceeded
  • Any rate-limit headers and retry guidance

docs.title: 7. Request and response conventions
docs.text:
The example uses these conventions:

  • HTTP methods describe the intended operation.
  • Query parameters are used to identify the requested rig.
  • JSON represents example request-independent response data.
  • Bearer authentication is illustrated through an HTTP header.
  • HTTP status codes communicate success or failure.

A production implementation should also define field validation, timestamp guarantees, units, nullability, data freshness, and the meaning of each possible status value.

docs.title: 8. Security and operational considerations
docs.text:
Telemetry can inform engineering decisions, so a real implementation requires controls beyond documenting an endpoint.

  • Enforce HTTPS and secure credential handling.
  • Authenticate and authorize callers.
  • Validate request parameters.
  • Define monitoring, logging, and error-handling requirements.
  • Document data freshness and measurement units.
  • Establish appropriate access controls and retention policies.
  • Verify all behaviour against the deployed service and approved engineering requirements.

Important: This API example is not a control system and must not be used to operate equipment, determine safe operating limits, or replace approved field procedures.

docs.title: 10. Scope and limitations
docs.text:
This reference demonstrates the structure and writing style of an API reference. It does not establish that an API implementation exists.

Before adapting this documentation for a real service, verify the base URL, authentication mechanism, endpoint behaviour, schemas, error responses, rate limits, and security requirements with the service owner and approved technical sources.
